title: Orbital Frost — Boardroom Keynote
description: A single dominant frosted slab floats over a deep spatial-navy field wrapped in an orbital gradient halo — built for executive product unveils where the title slide must feel as weighted and ceremonial as the announcement itself.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment before a product changes a room. It refuses visual collage, secondary accent colors, and any element that competes with the single message locked inside the glass card. The deep-space backdrop is not decoration — it is gravitational context that makes the frosted surface feel like it was placed there deliberately, at great cost. It is a design for speakers who command attention by subtraction.
goodFor: Single hero tagline or mission-statement moments
VisionOS and spatial computing product pitches
avoidFor: Multi-column comparison tables or data grids
Casual team standups or internal workshop decks
Academic citations requiring dense inline footnotes
author: harness

examples.promptCore: A single frosted glass slab levitates at the ceremonial center of a boundless deep-space void, as though placed there with deliberate, irreversible intent — the slide should feel like a curtain lifting in a darkened auditorium. The orbital halo is not a decoration but a gravitational exhale of ambient light that makes the frosted surface appear chosen rather than placed. Composition is perfectly centered and radially still, with vast negative space on all sides that forces every eye to the card without effort. Avoid any texture layering, secondary glow sources, decorative geometry, or peripheral elements that fracture the singular authority of the glass.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <defs>
    <radialGradient id="voidBg" cx="50%" cy="42%" r="78%">

      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#5fc8d6" stop-opacity="0"/>
    </radialGradient>
    <radialGradient id="haloInner" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">

      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#e8f4f8" stop-opacity="0.55"/>
      <stop offset="50%" stop-color="#7a98ad" stop-opacity="0.25"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#5fc8d6" stop-opacity="0.35"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="topSheen" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#e8f4f8" stop-opacity="0.32"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#e8f4f8" stop-opacity="0"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="titleGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">

    <filter id="soft" x="-20%" y="-20%" width="140%" height="140%">

  </defs>

  <!-- Deep space backdrop -->
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#0c2233"/>
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="url(#voidBg)"/>

  <!-- Orbital halo: gravitational exhale centered on card's upper midpoint -->
  <g opacity="0.95">
    <ellipse cx="960" cy="360" rx="900" ry="520" fill="url(#halo)"/>
    <ellipse cx="960" cy="360" rx="520" ry="320" fill="url(#haloInner)"/>
  </g>

  <!-- Subtle thin orbital ring (single, ambient) -->
  <ellipse cx="960" cy="360" rx="760" ry="430" fill="none" stroke="#5fc8d6" stroke-opacity="0.12" stroke-width="1"/>
  <ellipse cx="960" cy="360" rx="640" ry="360" fill="none" stroke="#e8f4f8" stroke-opacity="0.06" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- Glass card shadow -->
  <rect x="380" y="220" width="1160" height="640" rx="22" ry="22" fill="#0c2233" opacity="0.55" filter="url(#bigBlur)"/>

  <!-- Frosted glass card: columns 3-10, centered -->
  <g>
    <!-- Frosted body -->
    <rect x="380" y="220" width="1160" height="640" rx="22" ry="22" fill="#7a98ad" fill-opacity="0.10"/>
    <rect x="380" y="220" width="1160" height="640" rx="22" ry="22" fill="url(#glassFill)"/>
    <!-- Top inner sheen -->
    <rect x="382" y="222" width="1156" height="180" rx="20" ry="20" fill="url(#topSheen)"/>
    <!-- Edge stroke -->
    <rect x="380.5" y="220.5" width="1159" height="639" rx="21.5" ry="21.5" fill="none" stroke="url(#glassEdge)" stroke-width="1"/>
    <!-- Inner highlight stroke -->
    <rect x="384" y="224" width="1152" height="632" rx="18" ry="18" fill="none" stroke="#e8f4f8" stroke-opacity="0.10" stroke-width="1"/>
    <!-- Faint top highlight line -->
    <line x1="430" y1="221" x2="1490" y2="221" stroke="#e8f4f8" stroke-opacity="0.55" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#soft)"/>
  </g>

  <!-- Card content: title + subtitle, scale-only hierarchy -->
  <g font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" text-anchor="middle">
    <!-- Eyebrow micro-label -->
    <text x="960" y="430" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="18" letter-spacing="14" fill="#5fc8d6" opacity="0.85">ORBITAL FROST  ·  Q2 KEYNOTE  ·  MMXXVI</text>

    <!-- Title -->
    <text x="960" y="560" font-size="120" font-weight="400" fill="url(#titleGrad)" letter-spacing="-2">The Quiet Arrival</text>

    <!-- Subtitle -->
    <text x="960" y="650" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="300" fill="#e8f4f8" opacity="0.85" letter-spacing="2">A single instrument, engineered to change the room it enters.</text>

    <!-- Speaker / occasion line, far smaller, hierarchy by scale alone -->
    <text x="960" y="760" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#7a98ad" letter-spacing="6">PRESENTED BY THE OFFICE OF THE CHIEF DESIGNER  ·  APRIL  ·  TWENTY TWENTY-SIX</text>
  </g>
</svg>
examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; the frosted glass card spans columns 3–10 and is locked to the vertical and horizontal center of the canvas with generous breathing room on all four sides. The deep-space backdrop bleeds edge-to-edge with no crop or frame. The orbital gradient halo sits behind the card as a diffuse ambient ring centered on the card's upper midpoint — structurally invisible but perceptually gravitational. Title occupies the upper interior of the card, subtitle sits directly beneath it; hierarchy is established through scale contrast alone, with no rule lines, dividers, logo lock-ups, or page numbers anywhere on the canvas.

examples.promptCore: The content slide feels like a sealed chamber of deliberate information — each block placed with the quiet authority of a signed directive. The frosted surface contains the message rather than merely frames it, while the deep spatial backdrop holds its gravitational weight uninterrupted behind. Items read as spaced, weighted declarations with generous breathing room between them, never competing for hierarchy through decoration. Avoid icon clusters, secondary accent moments, or any texture that fragments the single ceremonial register this template demands.

    <text x="1795" y="1040" font-size="28" fill="#e8f4f8" text-anchor="end" letter-spacing="2">07 / 24</text>

  <!-- Left-edge deck mark (outside card) -->
  <g font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" fill="#7a98ad">
    <text x="125" y="1040" font-size="12" letter-spacing="4" transform="rotate(-90 125 1040)">ORBITAL FROST — CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  </g>

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; the frosted glass card spans columns 2–11 and sits vertically centered with a slight upward bias, preserving the deep-space backdrop beneath. Content inside the card is organized as 2–3 discrete stacked blocks divided by hairline rules — not a bullet list. A minimal section index or label locks to the card's top-left interior edge. A page number anchors bottom-right, outside the card boundary, on the bare backdrop.
